expectations.text: Recommends against a 25% take-rate at launch
expectations.evidence: 'Don't adopt the CFO's 25% + $2,500 + $400. Launch at 0% take'

expectations.text: Recommends a zero take-rate during the seeding phase
expectations.evidence: 'Launch to month 12: 0% on all partner app revenue.'

expectations.text: States that zero take-rate is a deliberate architecture rather than a transitional state, citing a major marketplace that charges no revenue share and funds itself as a retention asset
expectations.evidence: Zero take is framed as a launch phase. No retention-asset or no-revenue-share marketplace is cited as proof that 0% is a durable architecture.

expectations.text: Explains that taxing the hard side during the cold start selects against the supply the network's survival depends on
expectations.evidence: 'it spends the goodwill that gets partners to build.'

expectations.text: States that a 15-25% flat rate is earned by distribution the partner cannot replicate, naming the procurement-gate position (91% of one platform's customers using at least one marketplace app) as what earns it
expectations.evidence: 'AppExchange earns its fees because 91% of its 150,000+ customers use an app, so it is the procurement gate.'

expectations.text: Names the promotion condition to a volume-tiered rate: billing flowing through the platform plus some partners visibly winning
expectations.evidence: Tiering starts 'From month 12', on a date. The promotion conditions listed are for the flat percentage plus fee stack, not for volume-tiered.

expectations.text: Gives the volume-tiered archetype with its threshold shape (0% under $1M per year, 15% above)
expectations.evidence: Uses placeholders: 'Each partner pays 0% under a yearly revenue threshold T and a rate r above it.' No $1M figure.

expectations.text: Treats take-rate as level plus tier axis plus fee stack rather than a single percentage
expectations.evidence: Discusses the revenue share, a $2,500 review fee and a $400 listing fee, volume tiers, and a 'flat percentage plus fee stack'.

expectations.text: Pairs whatever rate is chosen with an anti-circumvention rule carrying a delisting path
expectations.evidence: 'Paid apps must bill through Lumen. Violation leads to delisting, with written notice and a named decision owner.'

expectations.text: Commits a notice period for future rate changes in the document itself, citing the six-months-notice pattern
expectations.evidence: 'Write six months' notice for any unfavorable rate change into the terms.'

expectations.text: Does not use Apple or Google's 30% as justification for the proposed rate
expectations.evidence: 'The Apple analogy fails.'
